ai.title: base-deep agent prompt updates for git safety and skill curation
ai.summary: The base-deep agent prompt now explicitly instructs agents to preserve unrelated changes in the git status/diff, preventing accidental reverts of concurrent user work. Skill contribution guidelines are tightened with a HIGH BAR for non-obvious insights, strictly forbidding task-specific or run-specific details in `.agents/skills/` files. These changes apply to `agents/base2/base-deep.ts`, affecting how the agent handles repository state and long-term knowledge capture.

eli5.text: The AI assistant now leaves any of your other ongoing work in the repository untouched instead of accidentally undoing it when it gets a new task. A new reminder in its instructions explicitly tells it to preserve unrelated changes sitting in your git status. The helper also tightens the rules for the shared tips it saves for future use: only broadly useful insights make the cut, and it now strictly avoids writing anything tied to the specific feature or run just completed, so the saved knowledge stays relevant across many different situations. The guidance is part of the assistant's base instructions today.

ai.title: Allow dated OpenRouter variants in free mode model checks
ai.summary: isFreeModeAllowedAgentModel now accepts dated model variants (e.g., minimax/minimax-m2.5-20260211) in addition to exact matches. The check iterates allowedModels to verify if the returned model string starts with an allowed base name followed by a hyphen. This change affects the core free-agents.ts constant file. It prevents false negatives when OpenRouter returns versioned model identifiers.

eli5.text: If you use the service in free mode, the system now correctly recognizes when OpenRouter returns a model name that includes a date suffix. Previously, a model like minimax/minimax-m2.5-20260211 would be rejected even though it's allowed, because the check only looked for an exact name match. Now, the system also accepts any model whose name starts with an approved base name followed by a hyphen, so versioned variants like this one are no longer blocked. This fix prevents legitimate free-mode usage from being incorrectly denied.

ai.title: Add OpenAI token counting to web API
ai.summary: Implemented `countTokensViaOpenAI` in `web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts` to handle token counting for OpenAI models via the Responses API. The logic detects OpenAI providers using `isOpenAIProviderModel`, converts message formats to Responses API input structures, and calls `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses/input_tokens`. Anthropic counting remains the default for non-OpenAI models. Scope is limited to the web API endpoint.

eli5.text: The token-counting tool now uses OpenAI's own counting service when you ask it to count tokens for an OpenAI model, instead of always using Anthropic's service for every model. If you send a prompt and specify an OpenAI model, the system checks whether that model comes from OpenAI and, if so, sends the request to OpenAI's endpoint to get the token count; otherwise, it falls back to the existing Anthropic-based counting. You would notice this because the logs now record whether the count came from OpenAI or Anthropic, and the error message no longer says "Anthropic" specifically when something goes wrong. This is live today and affects anyone using the internal token-count API endpoint.

ai.title: base-deep-evals agent added for BuffBench
ai.summary: New `base-deep-evals` agent definition created in `agents/base2/base-deep-evals.ts`. This variant uses `createBaseDeep({ noAskUser: true })` to disable the `ask_user` tool and related system prompt instructions. `evals/buffbench/main.ts` updated to run `base-deep-evals` instead of `base-deep`.

eli5.text: The automated grading harness that scores the assistant during internal evals now runs against a special variant of the assistant that has the 'ask me for help' tool turned off. This stops the assistant from interrupting those automated tests by asking follow-up questions. When you run the benchmark it now uses this question-free version, so it finishes tasks on its own instead of pausing to double-check with you.

ai.title: Add noLearning flag to base-deep agent
ai.summary: Adds `noLearning` boolean parameter to `buildDeepSystemPrompt` and `buildDeepInstructionsPrompt` in `agents/base2/base-deep.ts`. When true, Phase 7 (Lessons) is omitted from the system prompt example and the instructions prompt dynamically adjusts the workflow phase count to 6. The `base-deep-evals` agent definition in `agents/base2/base-deep-evals.ts` now passes `noLearning: true` alongside `noAskUser`.

eli5.text: The assistant now has an option to skip its final 'lessons learned' step, where it normally writes a takeaways file and updates its knowledge base after finishing a task. This only affects the version used to run coding competitions and evaluations, which turns that option on, so those runs stop one step earlier without writing the lessons file. If you looked at one of those runs, you'd notice it ends after validating results and never produces the lessons document.

ai.title: Disable OpenAI token counting in token-count API
ai.summary: The `useOpenAI` flag in `web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts` is hardcoded to `false`, bypassing `isOpenAIProviderModel`. This forces all token count requests to use `countTokensViaAnthropic` regardless of the model. The OpenAI import was removed as it is no longer used.

eli5.text: All requests to count how many tokens a message uses are now always routed through Anthropic's method, even if the model belongs to another provider. You would notice this only if you were measuring token counts programmatically against the API, where previously some provider-specific models may have used a different counting path. This is live today as a behind-the-scenes switch with no visible impact to end users.

ai.title: Fix markdown table alignment in knowledge-files.mdx docs
ai.summary: Aligned column widths in the 'When to Use Home Directory vs Project Knowledge Files' table in web/src/content/knowledge-files.mdx. Purely cosmetic fix to improve source readability. No functional changes to the rendered documentation or application logic.

eli5.text: The table that compares when to use your personal settings file versus your project settings file now has evenly spaced columns, so the text lines up neatly from row to row. This only affects how the documentation looks in the source file; the published page already displayed correctly and continues to do so. Nothing about how the files work or what they control has changed.

ai.title: Add meta skill and session artifacts for console log
ai.summary: Added `.agents/skills/meta/SKILL.md` with validation heuristics and session artifacts (`LESSONS.md`, `PLAN.md`, `SPEC.md`) for a CLI startup log change. The meta skill codifies patterns like using `bun run --cwd` and checking `git diff` scope. These files document the process of adding `console.log('Codebuff CLI starting')` to `cli/src/index.tsx`.

eli5.text: When the Codebuff command-line tool starts up, it now prints a single line of text to your terminal: "Codebuff CLI starting". This line appears immediately before any other startup messages and before the tool processes whatever command you gave it (like --help or login), so you'll see it every time the tool runs. The change is live now and only adds this one line; nothing else about how the tool works has changed.

ai.title: Add GPT-5.3, Claude-4.6, Gemini-3, Grok-4.1, GLM-5 to ModelName
ai.summary: ModelName union type updated to include new AI models: openai/gpt-5.3, openai/gpt-5.3-codex, anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6, anthropic/claude-opus-4.6, google/gemini-3-pro-preview, google/gemini-3-flash-preview, x-ai/grok-4.1-fast, z-ai/glm-5, and minimax/minimax-m2.5. Removed deprecated google/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025, google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-09-2025, and x-ai/grok-4-07-09. Changes applied to .agents/types/agent-definition.ts, agents/types/agent-definition.ts, and common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts.

eli5.text: The system that manages your AI assistant settings now recognizes the newest versions of popular AI models (GPT-5.3, Claude-4.6, Gemini-3, Grok-4.1, GLM-5) plus a couple of other updated options. Older, outdated model names were removed. You probably won't notice this directly, but agents that get updated soon can now choose these newer models when you pick which AI you'd like to run a task. This is in place today and ready to enable those model options moving forward.

ai.title: Upgrade file picker and lister to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite
ai.summary: File explorer agents now use google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview. The file-lister replaces x-ai/grok-4.1-fast, while the file-picker's max mode switches from grok-4.1-fast to the new model. Standard mode remains google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite. Updates affect agents/file-explorer/file-lister.ts and agents/file-explorer/file-picker.ts.

eli5.text: The built-in helper that searches your project for relevant files now uses a newer, faster Google AI model instead of the previous Grok model. You may notice slightly quicker results when that file-search helper scans directories, especially in its thorough mode; the standard mode stays the same. This rolls out today for anyone using that file finder inside the agent tools.

ai.title: file-picker max mode spawns single file-lister-max agent
ai.summary: Added file-lister-max.ts and updated file-picker.ts to spawn this single agent in max mode, replacing the previous parallel spawn of two file-lister agents. The new agent is configured to list up to 20 relevant files, whereas the standard file-lister remains capped at 12. This change consolidates the max-mode file discovery into a dedicated agent definition with updated prompts and spawn logic.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to look for the most relevant files in a project and you've asked for the biggest, most thorough search, it now looks through roughly twice as many files as before, about 20 instead of 12. Previously, that deep search sent out two separate file-finders at the same time, which could feel scattered; now it uses one dedicated searcher that is better instructed to focus and find the most relevant files. If you request a full scan of a codebase, you will get a longer, more focused list of files back. This only applies when you explicitly choose the most thorough search option, not during regular file lookups.

ai.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite replaces Grok in default agents
ai.summary: Default agent definitions and free-mode constants migrate from x-ai/grok models to google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview. This updates Commander, Researcher, Notion, and file exploration agents to use the new Gemini model for cost and latency efficiency. Changes span .agents/, agents/, common/src/constants/, and SDK documentation/examples. The researcher-web.ts file includes minor type casting formatting adjustments.

eli5.text: The default AI helpers built into the software no longer use xAI's Grok models and now use Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite instead. This swap means the Commander, Researcher, Notion, and file exploration tools switch to the Gemini model, likely for lower cost and faster response. If you open the program today, the difference you'd notice is that these agents silently route through the new Gemini model instead of Grok when performing tasks.

ai.title: CLI version bumped to 1.0.624
ai.summary: The CLI package version in `cli/release/package.json` has been incremented from 1.0.623 to 1.0.624 as part of a routine release-bump. This version increment captures a day's worth of upstream changes across the Freebuff monorepo, including the addition of the base-deep-evals agent for BuffBench, the noLearning flag for base-deep, OpenAI token counting in the web API (temporarily disabled and then removed), updated model definitions including GPT-5.3 and Gemini-3, and migrations of default agents to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite. The release packages these notable and minor changes into a new CLI revision, though the diff itself contains only the one-line version update.
ai.evidence: Modified file `cli/release/package.json` with a single-line version bump from 1.0.623 to 1.0.624 in the CLI package manifest, as specified in `release-bump` commit metadata.

eli5.text: This release sharpens the autonomous coding agent's workflow and refreshes the AI model lineup you can call on. The deep agent now follows a strict, self-checking build-and-review cycle (plan, write specs, implement, review, validate, learn) so changes are safer and lessons get captured automatically. File-finding tools were consolidated into a single smarter agent that surfaces up to 20 relevant files instead of spawning multiple searches. You gain access to newly listed models like GPT-5.3 and Gemini-3, while dated OpenRouter variants no longer trip up free-mode eligibility checks. Web token-counting for OpenAI models was added to the API, giving more accurate cost estimates for OpenAI-backed requests. Upgrading gives you a sturdier, opinionated agent that guards your existing work and a fresher model catalog for faster, cheaper task execution.

ai.title: Remove colon from session directory name
ai.summary: Session directory naming convention updated to replace colons with empty strings. Affected files include `.agents/sessions/` paths, `.agents/skills/meta/SKILL.md`, and `agents/base2/base-deep.ts`. This prevents filesystem issues with special characters in directory names.

eli5.text: Folders that store individual coding tasks now get created without a colon (:) in their name. If an assistant follows the standard checklist of steps, you would see folder names like "03-03-0909-add-console-log" instead of "03-03-09:09-add-console-log". The colon was removed because it can cause problems on some computer file systems, so the naming rule was changed to avoid it.

ai.title: CLI version 1.0.625
ai.summary: Bump CLI package version to 1.0.625 in cli/release/package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you use the coding assistant from the command line, updating to the latest version means your saved work sessions will no longer have colons in their folder names, which avoids errors on some computers. That is the most noticeable change; the rest of the update is just a behind-the-scenes refresh to keep everything running smoothly. Nothing else looks different to you unless you noticed those weird folder names.
